caption: The drawing is a black and white technical illustration rendered on an off-white or light beige background. It depicts an "Old City Street Lamp," as labeled in capital letters near the bottom center. The lamp is attached to an ornate metal bracket structure anchored to a wall with three circular mounting plates, each with bolts. The bracket is composed of thick, textured rods forming a pattern of loops, spirals, and decorative curls. The rod rises from the lower left, curves with a spiral to the upper left, and then extends to the upper right, ending in another spiral above the lamp. A circular flower-shaped ornament is positioned near the top left attachment point. The street lamp itself hangs down from the outermost right section of the bracket, featuring a rounded, downward-facing bell-shaped shade with linear detailing and a decorative edge. Measurements are included: the bracket and lamp assembly extends 24 inches horizontally from the wall and is 29 inches in vertical length. The illustration is enclosed within a rectangular border with ample space around the main drawing.
title: City Gas Light Bracket
cluster: #16 — Lighting Devices: Lamps, Lanterns, and Candleholders
